cards.q: Socratic method. 1) The three steps (1–2 words each)? 2) A case that meets the definition but isn't the thing shows it is not: n / s? 3) A case that is the thing but fails the definition shows it is not: n / s? 4) Name the productive dead end (1 word).
cards.a: (1) Get a definition. (2) Test it with a counterexample. (3) Accept that the definition fails, or refine it, and repeat until aporia (a productive dead end). A case that meets the definition but isn't the thing (enemy ran first; staying out of cowardice) shows the definition is not sufficient. A case that is the thing but fails the definition (leaving the post to rescue a friend) shows it is not necessary. A definition claims both directions.

cards.q: Arrow: no revocation → embassy stays open. Write: 1) converse 2) inverse 3) contrapositive. 4) Which one is equivalent?
cards.a: Converse (swap): embassy stays open → no revocation. Inverse (negate both in place): revocation → embassy doesn't stay open. cards.q: If A then B. Valid or invalid, and name: 1) A, so B 2) not B, so not A 3) B, so A 4) not A, so not B
cards.a: (1) Affirming the antecedent: valid. (2) Denying the consequent: valid (the contrapositive). (3) Affirming the consequent: invalid (converse). (4) Denying the antecedent: invalid (inverse). cards.q: "Most" + "most" of one group of 30. 1) Must some be in both? y/n 2) Smallest 'most' of 30? 3) Minimum overlap (show the sum)? 4) Does 'most + some' force overlap? y/n
cards.a: Yes. "Most" = MORE than half, so the two groups together count more than the whole group, and the excess must be counted twice. Smallest "most" of N is the first whole number above N/2 (30 → 16). Minimum overlap = most + most − N: 16 + 16 − 30 = 2. Odd N → 1, even N → 2. Only works for the SAME group; "most + some" forces nothing.

cards.q: Melian Dialogue. 1) Athens' position (≤8 words)? 2) Athens' reply to each Melian appeal: fair play → ?, the gods → ?, Sparta → ? (1–3 words each) 3) Does Thucydides endorse it? y/n 4) What follows next (2 words)?
cards.a: Athens: the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must; justice is talked about only between equals (realism). The Melians appeal to (1) fair play as Athens' own long-term interest, (2) the gods, (3) Spartan help. Athens answers: (1) its subjects are watching, so sparing Melos would look like weakness (reputation); (2) gods and men both rule wherever they can; (3) hope is the comfort of the desperate (Sparta acts on its own interest, not on kinship). Melos refuses; no help comes; Athens kills the men and enslaves the rest. cards.q: 1) Opposite of 'translator OR legal adviser'? 2) Opposite of 'closed AND evacuated'? 3) Plain 'or' allows both? y/n

Chain: worked 3 years → completed the course → night shift; add "anyone who has worked over a year completes the course" (or "Priya completed the course"). River picture: the premises leave you on one bank, the rule is one stepping stone, the bridge is the missing stone (the chain rule, C023). A sweeping rule is fine if it delivers; the traps are the converse/inverse and answers that are only necessary. Links: C028 (necessary), C030, C058.

cards.q: Bike lanes painted, sales fell 8%; owners blame the lanes; removing them will restore sales. 1) Main conclusion? 2) General gap (≤10 words)? 3) Is 'other streets did not fall similarly' necessary? y/n

The deficit (flow) fell by a third, but the debt (stock) still rose by 1 trillion; debt falls only when the flow turns negative (a surplus). cards.a: 12 = 2^2*3, 18 = 2*3^2. GCD = lowest power of each SHARED prime = 2*3 = 6 (biggest square tile for a 12x18 floor). LCM = highest power of EVERY prime = 2^2*3^2 = 36 (two lights flashing every 12 and 18 s meet at 36). Check: GCD*LCM = product (6*36 = 216 = 12*18). Remainder: n = 6k + 4 (k full cartons of 6 plus 4 loose eggs); n + 5 gives 9 loose = one more carton + 3, so remainder 3. Work with the remainder part only. QC: compute both columns before comparing (GCD of 36 and 60 = 12 vs LCM of 3 and 4 = 12: equal).

cards.q: A and B go together; the author says A causes B. 1) The four rivals to rule out (1–2 words each)? 2) Regression to the mean is a form of which rival? 3) General gap (≤6 words)?
cards.a: Five explanations: (1) A causes B (the claim); (2) reverse: B causes A; (3) common cause: C causes both; (4) reporting/measurement: the data is collected differently where A is present; (5) coincidence/chance: small or unrepresentative sample. A causal argument assumes 2-5 are false; weaken it by raising one, strengthen it by ruling one out. General gap: nothing else explains it / the cause is the one that was changed. Regression to the mean: a group picked for an extreme score (lowest 10 schools) tends to score closer to average next time by chance alone, so a rise after a program may be no effect of the program. Link: C062 (bike lanes), C068.

cards.q: 1) The two loop types? 2) Ring test: count ___ arrows; even = ?, odd = ? 3) A delay in a balancing loop causes (≤3 words)? 4) Bank run / thermostat: which type each?
cards.a: Reinforcing (R): a change feeds itself and runs away (bank run, compound interest). Balancing (B): a change triggers a response that pushes back toward a goal (thermostat, price). Test: trace the ring and count 'more -> less' (opposite) arrows: even (incl. zero) = reinforcing, odd = balancing. A delay in a balancing loop makes the response arrive late, so it overshoots and swings (boom and bust: housing built on today's rents, the shower tap, the Fed's lagged rate hikes). Dampen it by shortening the delay or showing the pipeline. Link: loops act on the flows into a stock (E6); in a loop A causes B and B causes A (L9).

cards.q: 1) −3² = ? (−3)² = ? 2) 2⁻¹ = ? 3) √75 = ? √48 = ? 4) 16^(1/2) = ? 5) Does a negative exponent make a number negative? y/n
cards.a: Multiply: add exponents (2^3*2^2 = five 2s = 2^5). Divide: subtract. Zero: a^0 = 1 (2^3/2^3). Negative: flip to the bottom, 2^-3 = 1/2^3; it NEVER makes the number negative. Power of a power: multiply exponents. (a) -3^2 = -(3^2) = -9 (the minus is x -1 outside); (-3)^2 = 9. (b) 2^-1 = 1/2. (c) Pairs picture: a root lets one of each PAIR of identical factors out front: 75 = 5*5*3 -> 5*sqrt(3); 48 = 4*4*3 -> 4*sqrt(3). Take the ROOT of the perfect square (sqrt16 = 4, not 16; sqrt25 = 5). (d) 16^(1/2) = sqrt16 = 4. Write every line on paper.

cards.q: 'No hospital qualifies without reporting every incident; Westbrook reports every incident; so it qualifies.' 1) Flaw: treats ___ as ___? 2) 'Only those who pass earn a star; Casa earned one, so it passed': valid / flawed? 3) 'Passing earns a star; Casa didn't earn one, so it didn't pass': valid / flawed?
cards.a: Flaw: treats a NECESSARY condition (reports every incident) as SUFFICIENT. A parallel choice starts from the necessary condition being met ('kitchen passes every inspection') and concludes the result ('will earn a star'). Valid look-alikes: 'only restaurants that pass earn a star; Casa earned a star, so it passes' (starts from the result: valid); 'a restaurant that passes will earn a star; Casa did not, so it did not pass' (denies the result of a sufficient condition: valid contrapositive); a probabilistic ('usually ... probably') version. Read all five choices on Level 3-4 items.

cards.q: Machiavelli, ch. 17. 1) The claim with its hedge (≤12 words)? 2) Why love fails (≤6 words)? 3) What the feared ruler must avoid (1 word), and the two things he must not touch?
cards.a: Both love and fear if possible; since they are hard to combine, it is much safer to be feared than loved IF one of the two has to be lacking (dropping the hedge misstates him). Reason: love is a link of obligation that men break whenever it pays them (self-interest, not passion); fear is a dread of punishment that never fails (it changes the payoff). Limit: avoid HATRED: the feared ruler must keep his hands off his subjects' property and women (men forget a father's death sooner than a lost inheritance).
